name: Checkerboard
summary: A grid of squares in two alternate colours, on a floor, in a picture or on a surface.
how: Use squares of one size: 300 to 600mm on a floor, or 1/8 to 1/16 of the width of a picture.
Lay the grid at 45° to make a small room look wider, or at 0° to show the vanishing point.

origin.note: Squares of two colours of marble pave Italian church floors and palace halls.

adoptions.via: Leon Battista Alberti builds the perspective of a picture on a squared pavement in De pictura.
Black and white floors pave Art Deco halls, bars and bathrooms.
Dorothy Draper lays black-and-white marble floors in hotel lobbies and halls.
Checker rugs, tiles and painted floors become a motif of colourful rooms.
